doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

title: The Sopranos and a mention of the Philly Sound
summary: Rowe and Gold chat about rewatching The Sopranos; Gold practices cello while watching and explains the show's Philly Sound reference and Columbia Records mob joke.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Okay. I'm trying to think of an anecdote, oh yes, this is a little odd. I've been watching re—runs of "The Sopranos."

Me too. I just finished as a matter of fact and it's like — it's my second time without my wife to watch it. And what I do is I actually play the cello — I know the dialogue a lot now so I will play scales and I'll play, you know I'm like working on a few new pieces. My hands hurt. But I'm trying my best you know, with my time, you know I make myself work on music for three or four hours a day no matter what the day may entail like I did when I was little. I mean, you know,
There was character called Christopher, you know Christopher, and there's one session/episode where —
Yeah. He mentions the Philly Sound and he was like, "Well I know music —" blah blah blah, and he mentions the Philly Sound.

Well actually what he says was, "The mob's been tied in to the record business forever and he starts mentioning certain names and everything and then he throws in the Philly Sound, which believe it or not, and I'm not going to say it, but the only mob activity the Philly Sound had was via Columbia Records.
